fixtures.preview: United host Bournemouth on Sunday 2pm UK time, three days after a 4-1 Champions League thrashing at Como that has put Michael Carrick under heavy pressure.
talking_points: United are winless in seven games in all competitions (three draws, four losses) and conceded inside two minutes in back-to-back European games.
They sit 13th on 7 points from 7 league games (one win, four draws, two losses); Bournemouth are 15th on 6 points.
Carrick called the Como performance 'unacceptable' and said 'it stops with me'; his job is under scrutiny.
Matthijs de Ligt made his first start in 325 days at Como, but injury and suspension news for Sunday isn't confirmed yet.

fixtures.preview: A 12:30pm UK lunchtime trip to Stamford Bridge, moved from the 3pm slot for UK TV.
Matchday 4 of the Champions League league phase brings Roma to Old Trafford, with United 20th in the table on 3 points from 3 games.
A Sunday 4:30pm UK home game against Aston Villa, picked for TV.
A trip to Anfield on 22 November; the kick-off time hasn't been set, so 12:00 UK is a placeholder.
Sydney's second game of the season, at home on Sunday afternoon after a 0-0 derby draw with the Wanderers.
talking_points: Sydney drew 0-0 with Western Sydney in front of 30,103 at Allianz Stadium on 16 October and sit 6th on 1 point.
Adelaide hadn't played a league game as of the 18 October ladder, so this may be their season opener.
Patrick Kisnorbo is Sydney's head coach; no team news for Sunday was found.
Sydney's Australia Cup run ended with a 0-2 semi-final loss to Melbourne Victory on 9 September.

fixtures.preview: A 5pm Halloween game at AAMI Park, Melbourne City's home opener.

notes: Searches were thin and many sites blocked access (HTTP 403/429), so several sections are shorter than their limits rather than padded.

Man Utd: the 4-1 loss at Como is from Sky Sports; the league position (13th) is from Wikipedia and MUFC Review. Bournemouth injury and suspension news isn't out yet. The Chelsea, Roma, Villa and Liverpool details are carried over or from schedule listings only, and the Liverpool kick-off time isn't set.

Sydney FC: Wikipedia's fixture table omits the Mariners (6 Nov) and Brisbane (21 Nov) games, which come from Austadiums and the A-Leagues fixture guide. The Mariners time is from a non-official source, and the 6 Dec Victory time is from Wikipedia only. No Adelaide team news was found.

Big matches: the Bayern v Arsenal and Real Madrid v Leipzig games on 21 Oct are over or in progress and were dropped. Stan Sport has the Premier League and Champions League and beIN Sports has LaLiga, but I found nothing confirming the El Clásico broadcast specifically. The Wallabies v England Test (8 Nov) was left out because no Australian broadcaster was confirmed.

Live sport: Kings times (3pm Sunday) come from the Kings ticketing page via search results and weren't opened directly. No Matildas, Socceroos or Waratahs home games in the next 4 weeks could be confirmed, and no tennis in Sydney is in the window.
Local: no local news from the past 7 days was found, South Eveleigh's events page returned no 2026 content, and no Term 4 events were found on the schools' public sites.

Not found: Pokémon, Minecraft or Roblox events in Sydney, a confirmed junior or kids' run near home (the Fisher's Ghost Fun Run at Campbelltown on 8 Nov has a 5km open to ages 7+, but 2026 details weren't confirmed), Sydney matcha pop-ups with current dates, football-boot or running-shoe sales (Rebel's Mid Season Sale ended 11 Oct), and ticket deals for kids' shows.

Groceries: the Woolworths and Coles half-price lists for the 21 Oct week weren't accessible, so most items show a special price with no was-price. The Aldi tuna price comes from the Spring catalogue, which runs to 30 Nov.
Deals: items come from the OzBargain front page, with prices and expiries as listed there. Previous-run deals that couldn't be re-checked were dropped.
